claims.text: The identity of X is the primary control on protective oxide-scale stability above 900 °C in CrFeCoNiX alloys.
CrFeCoNiAl forms a slow-growing protective oxide scale.
CrFeCoNiSi forms a slow-growing protective oxide scale.
The protective scale on CrFeCoNiAl is dominated by Al2O3.
The protective scale on CrFeCoNiSi is dominated by Si-rich oxide phases.
Al- and Si-bearing scales are coherent and adherent, accommodate thermal stress, and thereby minimize cracking and spallation.
CrFeCoNiMn forms a more volatile oxide scale.
Poor adhesion and a larger thermal-expansion mismatch cause stress accumulation, cracking, and spallation in the Mn-bearing alloy.
The hypothesis covers CrFeCoNiX alloys in either single-phase or multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
A 100-hour air-oxidation exposure at 950–1050 °C is suitable for comparing the Al-, Si-, and Mn-bearing alloys.
Oxide chemistry, oxide-scale coherence, oxide-metal interface quality, and thermal-expansion matching govern scale persistence.
Changing X modifies oxide-formation kinetics and scale adhesion.
A continuous Al- or Si-rich scale acts as a barrier resistant to cracking.
Differences in diffusion rates and resulting interfacial thermal stress mediate the effect of X on oxide stability.
Compared with CrFeCoNiMn, the Al- and Si-bearing alloys will have more uniform and adherent scales, slower thickening, and fewer cracks or spalls.
CrFeCoNiMn will exhibit higher oxidation mass gain than the Al- and Si-bearing alloys.
CrFeCoNiMn is an appropriate baseline for poor oxide stability because it is expected to form a less protective and more volatile scale.
Microstructural state and processing route can alter oxidation behavior in CrFeCoNiAl.
Grain refinement and an accompanying BCC/B2-to-FCC transformation reduce oxidation kinetics in AlCoCrFeNi under 850–1050 °C air exposure.
Failure of Al- and Si-bearing alloys to show significantly lower growth rates, fewer cracks or spalls, and greater adhesion than CrFeCoNiMn would falsify the proposed X-controlled mechanism.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis specifies temperatures above 900 °C, whereas the intervention and boundary include 900 °C through the notation ≥900 °C.
The proposed conditions describe the tests as isothermal while also requiring controlled thermal cycling; these are distinct exposure modes unless separate test stages are defined.
